title: Parameters, returns and passing values
goal: Explain passing an int by value and save the call result.

prerequisites.text: Distinguish a parameter from an argument in a function call.

terms.title: Parameter
terms.definition: A local object receiving an argument value.

terms.title: Return value
terms.definition: The result delivered to the call site.

sections.title: Why it matters
paragraphs: A log needs the original score after a bonus. The call supplies original’s value to a local score.
Assignment to score does not change original. The caller uses the return value to keep the new score.

sections.title: Worked example
paragraphs: Write both numbers the user will see after score changes.

sections.title: Diagnostics
paragraphs: A bare call can compile even when its result is ignored. Debug by comparing expected and observed output.
An int function needs a return value. Clang rejects return without an expression.

sections.title: Transfer to practice
paragraphs: A final price of zero is valid. Reject a discount exceeding the price before the call. Afterwards print both the original price and the result.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Explain passing an int by value and save the call result.

feedback: 15 is returned and the original is 9.
A parameter does not update original.

selfcheck.prompt: Where should a discarded result be fixed?
feedback: The int is already printed correctly.
The discount type matches the contract.

selfcheck.prompt: Why does original stay 9 when score changes?
selfcheck.feedback: They are distinct objects. The call copies original’s value and only modifies score.

diagnosticExercises.source:
static int score(void) { return; }
int main(void) { return score(); }

practice.title: Price before and after a discount
practice.task: Read price and discount from 0 to 100 on separate lines. If discount exceeds price, print invalid. Save the result of discounted_price and print it beside the original price. The supplied read_integer function checks the first two lines. A missing line, an invalid number or an out-of-range value gives invalid. The program ignores any later input.
practice.hint: The starter compiles. Find where the result is computed but discarded.

steps.action: Enter the price 40 and discount 5 on separate lines, then run the starter.
steps.why: Explain passing an int by value and save the call result.
steps.expected: The starter prints 40 40. The contract calls for the original price and the result, 40 35.

steps.action: Save the return value of discounted_price. Run again with the same input, then try matching price and discount.
steps.why: The change must satisfy the contract.
steps.expected: Inputs 40 and 5 give 40 35. Inputs 5 and 5 give 5 0.

steps.action: Check a distinct boundary case and explain the result.
steps.why: Different cases distinguish the parts of the rule.

exercises.title: Independent transfer
exercises.task: Predict the outcome if the result is saved into price and price is printed twice.
criteria: The original price is no longer stored separately.
